learn.title: Many ways to show data
learn.html:
We can show the same data in different ways:

📋 a table   📊 a bar graph   🥧 a pie chart

A pie chart is also called a circle graph.

Favorite petCatRabbitHamsterDog
Number of students20151040

learn.title: The same pets in a pie chart
learn.html:
Here is the same pet data as a pie chart.

The biggest slice is Dog (40). The smallest slice is Hamster (10).

More students = a bigger slice.

learn.title: What is a pie chart?
learn.html:
A pie chart is a circle cut into slices, like a pizza 🍕.

The whole circle is all the data.

Each slice (a sector) is one group. A bigger amount gets a bigger slice.

learn.title: Class 6F T-shirts
learn.html:
Color of T-shirtYellowGreenBlue
Number of students151510

Yellow and Green both have 15, so their slices are the same size.

Blue has only 10, so its slice is smaller.

learn.title: Tarts: pie charts with fractions
learn.html:
1/4 of the tarts are strawberry, 1/4 are chocolate and 1/2 are pineapple.

The whole circle is 1 whole, so all the fractions add up to 1:

1/4 + 1/4 + 1/2 = 1

The little square means a quarter of the circle (1/4).

learn.title: Janice: pie charts with percentages
learn.html:
Janice spent 40% of her pocket money on food and drinks and 20% on transport. She saved the rest.

The whole circle is 100%.

Savings = 100% - 40% - 20% = 40%

learn.title: Numbers, fractions or percentages
learn.html:
The same data can use numbers, fractions or percentages.

AdultsBoysGirlsTotal
Number604060160
Fraction60/160 = 3/840/160 = 1/460/160 = 3/81
Percentage37.5%25%37.5%100%

Fraction = part ÷ total. Percentage = fraction × 100%.

learn.title: Burgers (a) and (b)
learn.html:
Beef burgers is a quarter (1/4) of the circle and made 750 baht. Cheese burgers is also a quarter, so it made 750 baht.

4 quarters make the whole circle:

750 baht × 4 = 3,000 baht in total.

learn.title: Burgers (c) and (d)
learn.html:
Chicken + fish = 1 - 1/4 - 1/4 = 1/2 of the circle.

1/2 is 2 quarters: 750 baht × 2 = 1,500 baht.

Chicken is twice fish. Fish = 1 unit, chicken = 2 units, so 3 units = 1,500 baht.

Fish: 1,500 baht ÷ 3 = 500 baht. Chicken: 500 × 2 = 1,000 baht.

learn.title: Hands-On: make your own pie chart
learn.html:
Ask your classmates a question, like “What is your favorite hobby?”

Favorite pastimeNumber
Play computer games10
Watch TV8
Read15
Play ball games7

Type the table into a spreadsheet and make a pie chart. Then ask friends what it shows.

questions.label: Do and Learn (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of people in a theater on a weekend. (a) How many more men than women were there?
questions.hint: Find Men and Women on the pie chart. Take away the smaller number.
questions.answer: There were 15 more men than women.

questions.label: Do and Learn (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of people in a theater on a weekend. (b) How many people were in the theater?
questions.hint: Look at the little square on the Women slice. What part of the circle is it?
steps: The little square shows a right angle, so the Women slice is a quarter (1/4) of the circle.
questions.answer: There were 180 people in the theater.
questions.why: Women is 1/4 of the circle, so the total is 45 × 4 = 180.

questions.label: Do and Learn (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of people in a theater on a weekend. (c) How many girls were there?
questions.hint: Total people take away men, women and boys.
questions.answer: There were 20 girls.

questions.label: Exercise 1
questions.q:
The table shows the favorite colors of students in Class 6D.
ColorBlueGreenRedYellow
Number of students1015105
Tick ( ✓ ) the pie chart that shows the information in the table correctly.
questions.hint: Find the total. Then work out what fraction of the circle each color should be.
steps: So Green must be the biggest slice and Yellow the smallest. Blue and Red are each a quarter.
Chart A: Yellow (5) is bigger than Green (15). Wrong ✗
Chart B: Blue (10) is half of the circle. Wrong ✗
Chart C: Blue and Red are quarters, Green is biggest, Yellow is smallest. Right ✓
Chart D: 1/4, 1/4, 3/8 and 1/8. These are the right fractions. Right ✓
questions.answer: Charts C and D are correct. ✓
questions.why: Blue and Red are 1/4 each, Green is 3/8 and Yellow is 1/8. Only C and D show this.

questions.label: Exercise 2 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different levels of students from Primary 4 to Primary 6 who join the Chess Club in a school. (a) ___ Primary 6 students join the Chess Club.
questions.hint: Read the number written in the Primary 6 slice.
steps: The number written on it is 28.
questions.answer: 28 Primary 6 students join the Chess Club.
questions.why: The pie chart shows 28 for Primary 6.

questions.label: Exercise 2 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different levels of students from Primary 4 to Primary 6 who join the Chess Club in a school. (b) ___ Primary 4 students join the Chess Club.
questions.hint: Primary 4 and Primary 6 both have a little square. What does that tell you?
steps: Primary 6 and Primary 4 both have a right-angle mark, so each one is a quarter of the circle.
questions.answer: 28 Primary 4 students join the Chess Club.
questions.why: Both slices are quarters, so they are equal: 28.

questions.label: Exercise 2 (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different levels of students from Primary 4 to Primary 6 who join the Chess Club in a school. (c) ___ Primary 5 students join the Chess Club.
questions.hint: Primary 5 is half of the circle. Half = 2 quarters.
steps: Primary 4 + Primary 6 = 2 quarters = half of the circle.
questions.answer: 56 Primary 5 students join the Chess Club.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of different types of fish in an aquarium. (a) How many swordfish are there?
questions.hint: Read the number on the Swordfish slice.
questions.answer: There are 16 swordfish.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of different types of fish in an aquarium. (b) How many more angelfish than goldfish are there in the aquarium?
questions.hint: Angelfish take away goldfish.
questions.answer: There are 10 more angelfish than goldfish.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of different types of fish in an aquarium. (c) How many guppies are there?
questions.hint: The straight line cuts the circle into 2 halves. Angelfish and goldfish make one half.
steps: The straight line through the middle makes two halves.
The other half (Guppies + Swordfish) is also 50.
questions.answer: There are 34 guppies.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (d)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of different types of fish in an aquarium. (d) What fraction of the fish are guppies?
questions.hint: Fraction = guppies ÷ all the fish. Two halves of 50 make the whole.
steps: Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 2. 34 ÷ 2 = 17 and 100 ÷ 2 = 50.
questions.answer: 17/50 of the fish are guppies.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the percentages of buttons by color in a box. There are 100 blue buttons and green buttons altogether. The rest are yellow and red. There are twice as many red buttons as blue buttons. (a) What percentage of the buttons are red?
questions.hint: Red is twice blue. Blue is 10%.
steps: Red is twice as many as blue.
questions.answer: 20% of the buttons are red.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the percentages of buttons by color in a box. There are 100 blue buttons and green buttons altogether. The rest are yellow and red. There are twice as many red buttons as blue buttons. (b) What percentage of the buttons are yellow?
questions.hint: The whole circle is 100%. Take away the other colors.
questions.answer: 30% of the buttons are yellow.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the percentages of buttons by color in a box. There are 100 blue buttons and green buttons altogether. The rest are yellow and red. There are twice as many red buttons as blue buttons. (c) What is the total number of buttons in the box?
questions.hint: Blue and green together are 50%, and that is 100 buttons.
steps: 50% is half. The whole (100%) is 2 halves.
questions.answer: There are 200 buttons in the box.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (d)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the percentages of buttons by color in a box. There are 100 blue buttons and green buttons altogether. The rest are yellow and red. There are twice as many red buttons as blue buttons. (d) How many blue buttons are there?
questions.hint: Blue is 10% of 200.
questions.answer: There are 20 blue buttons.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (e)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the percentages of buttons by color in a box. There are 100 blue buttons and green buttons altogether. The rest are yellow and red. There are twice as many red buttons as blue buttons. (e) What is the ratio of the number of green buttons to the number of yellow buttons?
questions.hint: Use the percentages, then simplify.
questions.answer: The ratio is 4 : 3.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (f)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the percentages of buttons by color in a box. There are 100 blue buttons and green buttons altogether. The rest are yellow and red. There are twice as many red buttons as blue buttons. (f) Which are the two colors of buttons that make up 3/5 of the total number of buttons in the box?
questions.hint: Change 3/5 into a percentage. Then find two colors that add up to it.
questions.answer: Green and red buttons make up 3/5 of the box.

flash.back: A circle cut into slices to show data. Also called a circle graph.
One part of a pie chart. A bigger amount has a bigger slice.
1/4 = 25%. It has a little square (right angle) at the centre.
1/2 = 50%. A straight line through the centre cuts it in half.
Part ÷ total. Example: 40 boys out of 160 = 40/160 = 1/4.
Total take away all the other slices. Example: 100% - 40% - 20% = 40%.
If a quarter is 45, the whole is 45 × 4 = 180.
Same size slices show the same amount.

3/5 of the buttons is what percentage?

learn.title: Unit 14 big ideas
learn.html:
🥧 A pie chart shows parts of a whole.

Whole circle = 1 = 100%.

Little square = a quarter. Straight line through the centre = two halves.

Know one part? Use it to find the total, then the other parts.

learn.title: Units in a pie chart
learn.html:
Mary: Books 1/3, Transport 2/12, Food 1/12.

Make them all twelfths: Books 4/12, Transport 2/12, Food 1/12.

Clothes = 12/12 - 7/12 = 5/12.

Food 1 unit = 60 baht, so Clothes 5 units = 300 baht.

learn.title: Vertically opposite slices
learn.html:
When two straight lines cross at the centre, the opposite angles are equal.

Equal angles = equal slices. Apples is opposite Pineapples, so Apples = 50.

Another way: 3 quarters = 120 × 3 = 360. Oranges = 360 - 50 - 50 - 30 - 40 = 190.

learn.title: Math in Real Life: food waste
learn.html:
A survey asked 1,016 people about food waste. 90% feel it is a waste of money to throw food away.

Work in groups. Ask your class a question about food waste and make a pie chart of the answers.

questions.label: Let's Think Along (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows how Mary spent her pocket money last week. She spent 60 baht on food. (a) What fraction of her pocket money was spent on clothes?
questions.hint: The whole circle is 1. Take away the other fractions. Make them all twelfths first.
questions.answer: 5/12 of her pocket money was spent on clothes.

questions.label: Let's Think Along (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows how Mary spent her pocket money last week. She spent 60 baht on food. (b) How much money did she spend on clothes?
questions.hint: Food is 1/12, that is 1 unit = 60 baht. Clothes is 5/12, that is 5 units.
steps: Cut the circle into 12 equal units.
questions.answer: She spent 300 baht on clothes.

questions.label: Let's Think Along (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows how Mary spent her pocket money last week. She spent 60 baht on food. (c) Was the total amount she spent on books and food the same as the amount spent on clothes? Explain.
questions.hint: Count the units for books, food and clothes.
questions.answer: Yes. Books and food are 4 units + 1 unit = 5 units, the same as clothes (5 units).
questions.why: Both are 5/12 of her pocket money (300 baht).

questions.label: Performance Task (a)
questions.q:
In a survey, 320 children were asked to name their favorite desserts. The table shows the number of children who chose each type of dessert.
Type of dessertCakeTartCookiesIce cream
Number of children8020120100
Fraction????
(a) Work out the fraction of children who like each type of dessert and fill in the table.
questions.hint: Fraction = number of children ÷ 320. Then simplify.
steps: Cake: 80/320. Divide top and bottom by 80: 1/4
Tart: 20/320. Divide top and bottom by 20: 1/16
Cookies: 120/320. Divide top and bottom by 40: 3/8
Ice cream: 100/320. Divide top and bottom by 20: 5/16
questions.answer: Cake 1/4, Tart 1/16, Cookies 3/8, Ice cream 5/16
questions.why: Each number ÷ 320, simplified. They add up to 1 whole.

questions.label: Performance Task (b)
questions.q: Present the information in the given pie chart. Label the pie chart and use a different color for each type of dessert.
questions.hint: The circle has 16 equal parts. Each part is 1/16.
steps: Make the circle into 16 equal parts. Each part is 1/16.
questions.answer: Cake 4 parts, Tart 1 part, Cookies 6 parts and Ice cream 5 parts, each in a different color, as in the pie chart.
questions.why: Each fraction out of 16 tells you how many of the 16 parts to color.

questions.label: Problem Solving
questions.q: The pie chart shows the number of fruits sold at a fruit stall. How many oranges are there?
questions.hint: Mangoes has a little square, so it is a quarter. Pineapples, papayas and pears make the other quarter of that half.
steps: The straight line makes a half. That half is Pineapples, Papayas, Mangoes and Pears.
Mangoes is a quarter (1/4), so the rest of that half is 1/2 - 1/4 = 1/4.
So one quarter of the circle is 120 fruits.
The other half is Pineapples + Oranges = 240.
questions.answer: There are 190 oranges.
questions.why: A quarter is 120, so a half is 240. Pineapples + oranges = 240, so oranges = 240 - 50 = 190.

questions.label: Math Journal
questions.q: The pie chart shows information on the different types of footwear Mr Tay sold on a Sunday. Explain which bar graph below best represents the information in the pie chart.
questions.hint: Which slices are the same size? Which slice is the biggest?
steps: In the pie chart, Sandals and Boots are the same size (both are quarters).
So the Sandals and Boots bars must be the same height.
Dress shoes is the biggest slice, so its bar must be the tallest.
Bar Graph A: Boots is taller than Sandals. ✗
Bar Graph B: Sandals = Boots, and Dress shoes is tallest. ✓
questions.answer: Bar graph B. The pie chart shows the same number of sandals and boots sold, so their bars should be the same height. The bar for dress shoes should be the tallest, as the most dress shoes were sold.
questions.why: Same size slices = same height bars. Biggest slice = tallest bar.

flash.back: A circle cut into slices to show data. Also called a circle graph.
One part of a pie chart. A bigger amount has a bigger slice.
1/4 = 25%. It has a little square (right angle) at the centre.
1/2 = 50%. A straight line through the centre cuts it in half.
Part ÷ total. Example: 40 boys out of 160 = 40/160 = 1/4.
Change fractions to the same bottom number. 1/12 = 1 unit, 5/12 = 5 units.
Two straight lines cross: the opposite slices are the same size.
